Apple farming in India: the orchard guide

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

A practical orchard guide for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand and new low-chill areas: varieties and rootstocks, pollination, pruning, a fertilizer calculator for bigha, kanal and nali, fixing fruit drop and small fruit, saving dying trees, sprays, harvest and profit.

Apple farming in India in short: plant virus-indexed trees on a rootstock that suits your soil (never MM.106 in heavy clay), with 25–33% compatible pollinizers and 4–6 beehives per hectare at bloom. Standard Delicious needs 800–1,500 chilling hours below 7°C (about 1,500–2,700 m). Feed by tree age (Dr. YSP UHF: 70:35:70 g N:P₂O₅:K₂O per year of age, full 700:350:700 g from year 10), thin fruit at pea size, seal pruning cuts and keep water away from the trunk. Seedling orchards average 6–11 t/ha; clonal high-density orchards reach 30–45 t/ha and more.

Apple in India at a glance

India is the world's fifth-largest apple producer: about 297 thousand hectares and 2.69 million tonnes in 2024–25 (MoA&FW second advance estimates; USDA FAS forecasts 2.55 million tonnes). Jammu & Kashmir grows about 70%, Himachal Pradesh about 20–26%, Uttarakhand about 3%, with smaller areas in Arunachal Pradesh and the North-East.

Traditional seedling orchards average only 6–11 t/ha, against 30–45 t/ha and more in clonal high-density orchards (ICAR-CITH). Nearly 30% of Himachal's harvest is lost or downgraded after picking (NITI Aayog 2026), and 544,000–600,000 tonnes of imported apples a year press prices for small, poorly coloured Delicious (USDA FAS 2024). The money is in clean, well-coloured fruit above 70 mm.

Climate, chilling hours and site

Standard Delicious apples need 800–1,500 hours below 7°C (chilling hours), roughly 1,500–2,700 m altitude, 1,000–1,250 mm of rain and frost-free weather at bloom: below −2°C the flowers' pistils die (NHB, Himachal package of practices). In lower belts (4,000–6,500 ft) choose north or north-east slopes, which avoid winter sunscald, and high-colour strains; in high belts (6,500–8,000 ft and above) use south-east slopes. Warm valleys at 400–1,400 m can grow low-chill HRMN-99, Anna or Dorsett Golden. Anti-hail nets prevent hail damage and soften summer sunscald.

Soil

Apple needs deep, well-drained loam with pH 5.5–6.8 and organic carbon above 1.0%. Waterlogging in the June–September monsoon is the main trigger of white root rot, and wet clay kills MM.106 trees through collar rot. Below pH 5.5, use CAN or lime/dolomite rather than ammonium sulphate. Root rot and dying trees →

Varieties, rootstocks and pollination

Old orchards are mostly Royal or Red Delicious on seedling rootstock. New blocks use high-colour strains (Scarlet Spur-II, Red Chief, Super Chief, Oregon Spur, Jeromine, Red Velox) and Gala on clonal rootstocks (M.9, MM.106, MM.111, M.7), which bear in 2–3 years instead of 6–8. Every block needs 25–33% diploid pollinizers (Golden Delicious, Granny Smith, Redlum Gala, Fuji or Manchurian crabapple) flowering at the same time. Varieties and rootstocks →

Hill land units: 1 acre = 5 Himachal bighas (809.37 m² each) = 8 J&K kanals (505.86 m² each) = 20.16 Uttarakhand nalis (200.67 m² each). A 6 × 6 m orchard holds about 22 trees per Himachal bigha.

Pruning

Heavy heading cuts, shaded lower branches, narrow forks and unsealed stubs cause upright non-fruiting shoots, canker dieback, weak buds and alternate bearing. Use thinning cuts, remove limbs thicker than half the trunk with angled renewal cuts, bend branches to 45–60°, and paste every cut over 2.5 cm at once with copper oxychloride or Bordeaux paste. Pruning guide →

Irrigation

Even with 1,000–1,250 mm of rain, dry spells in May–June (cell division) and August–September (fruit sizing) shrink fruit and trigger bitter pit. On M.9 drip, give about 2–4 L per tree per day in early spring, 6–10 L in May–June and 10–15 L or more in July–August; drip saves 40–50% water (ICAR-CITH, SKUAST-K). A 10–15 cm organic mulch ring, kept 30 cm away from the trunk, cuts evaporation by over 30% and reduces collar rot from soil splash. Dry-then-flooded irrigation cracks fruit.

Fertilizer in one paragraph

Standard trees get 70 g N, 35 g P₂O₅, 70 g K₂O and 10 kg FYM per year of age until year 10; bearing trees take 700 : 350 : 700 g plus 70–100 kg FYM (Dr. YSP UHF, SKUAST-K). M.9 high-density trees get half that per year of age up to year 7, through weekly drip. FYM, all phosphorus and half the potash go in November–December; 60% of nitrogen 2–3 weeks before bud break; the rest after petal fall, and less of it in an off year. Calculate your orchard's dose →

The orchard year

MonthMain work
Dec–FebDormant pruning (thin out limbs over half trunk size), paste cuts over 2.5 cm, clear drainage ditches, FYM + phosphorus + potash
MarDormant horticultural mineral oil (2%) above 4°C and 14–21 days apart from sulphur; pre-bloom nitrogen (50–67%)
AprBoron at pink bud (0.1–0.15%); 4–6 beehives per hectare; no sprays at full bloom
MayThin fruit 10–25 days after petal fall; start 4–6 calcium chloride sprays; reduce nitrogen in an off year
Jun–AugIrrigate dry spells; summer pruning of water sprouts; watch root rot, Marssonina and mites in the monsoon
Aug–OctStop sprays 3–4 weeks before picking; NAA against pre-harvest drop if needed; harvest by starch-iodine test
Oct–Nov3–5% urea + 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.1–0.2% boron on green leaves; copper clean-up

Main problems by state

  • Jammu & Kashmir: overspending on pesticides, Marssonina and Alternaria leaf fall, white root rot, and the codling moth quarantine in Ladakh (SKUAST-K).
  • Himachal Pradesh: falling chill below 1,200 m, May–June drought, replant disease in old blocks, hail and about 30% post-harvest loss (Dr. YSP UHF, NITI Aayog 2026).
  • Uttarakhand: small hill holdings, canker and dieback from unsealed pruning cuts, root rot and cold-chain gaps.
  • Arunachal Pradesh and low-chill areas: high monsoon humidity, very acidic soils (pH below 5.2) needing lime and boron, and access to clean nursery plants.

Questions farmers ask

How much chilling does an apple tree need?

Standard Delicious apples need 800–1,500 hours below 7°C; Gala, Granny Smith and Fuji 700–1,000; low-chill HRMN-99, Anna and Dorsett Golden only 250–500.

How many apple trees are planted per acre?

63–72 in traditional seedling orchards, 112–162 at 5–6 m, 253–450 in medium density on MM.106 or MM.111, and 899–1,349 in M.9 high density.

How long does an apple tree take to bear fruit?

Seedling rootstocks take 6–8 years; clonal rootstocks such as M.9 and MM.106 bear in 2–3 years.

What is the yield of apple per hectare in India?

Traditional orchards average 6–11 t/ha; clonal high-density orchards reach 30–45 t/ha and more by year 5 (ICAR-CITH).

Why are my apple trees drying?

Most often white root rot in wet monsoon soil, collar rot on MM.106 in clay, canker from unsealed pruning cuts, or replant disease. See how to tell them apart.

Why do apple flowers drop without fruit?

Too few compatible pollinizers, too few bees, cold or rain at bloom, boron shortage or spraying during bloom. Plant 25–33% pollinizers and keep 4–6 beehives per hectare.

Which states grow apple in India?

Jammu & Kashmir (about 70%), Himachal Pradesh (about 20–26%) and Uttarakhand (about 3%), with smaller areas in Arunachal Pradesh and the North-East.

How many kanals or bighas are in an acre?

1 acre = 5 Himachal bighas = 8 J&K kanals = 20.16 Uttarakhand nalis.
